items.text: Amazon redesigned the Kindle — but this $35 accessory may steal the show
items.article: Amazon launched a redesigned Kindle lineup, but the standout might be the new $35 Kindle Click, a Bluetooth page-turning remote. See more of our coverage in your search results. As a longtime Kindle user, quite literally since the first generation, I’m always excited when there’s a new Kindle launch. I’m an author myself and an avid reader, and my current Kindle Colorsoft has hundreds of books loaded onto it. That said, even though my Kindles have truly survived the test of time (my oldest is close to 20 years old), I’m always excited when Amazon releases a new iteration. Today, the brand launched a completely redesigned Kindle family, starting with a brand-new 6-inch Kindle , a compact, pocketable device that feels built for people like me who are always on the go. The new Kindle has a flush-front display and a slimmer design, with the color of the device wrapping from front to back. The standard 16GB model comes in ube, a rich purple, and graphite, a classic gray, while a new 32GB aluminum version comes in alpine sky and seaglass green. This is the Kindle for you if you need something even more portable than the Paperwhite. It offers up to six weeks of battery life and Amazon says books open 30% faster than on the previous release. Plus, for the first time, the 6-inch Kindle is available with an aluminum back, giving the device a slightly more premium feel without sacrificing its pocket-sized design.

items.text: Met Office issues October snow verdict in new long-range forecast
items.article: Forecasters have also revealed where snow could fall if colder conditions develop across the UK. The Met Office has issued its verdict on the chances of snow hitting the UK in October. Britain basked in several scorching heatwaves over the summer that saw temperatures regularly top 35C, with several records also broken. The mercury has been dipping over the last couple of weeks, with glorious sunshine replaced by more downpours and stronger, colder winds. Despite this, Met Office forecasters have told the Express there are currently "no strong signals for widespread or disruptive snowfall across the UK during October". However, brief colder spells have not been ruled out , while the highest parts of Scotland would be the most likely areas to see snow if wintry conditions do develop. A spokesperson said: "The Met Office's latest outlook indicates a greater likelihood of temperatures being above average overall during the month, although this does not rule out the possibility of brief colder spells. Current guidance suggests the risk of impacts typically associated with early-season cold weather, such as widespread frost, ice or snowfall, is lower than normal." You agree you are 18 or over. Set us as preferred After enduring 30 Chicago winters, I gifted myself my Hollywood dream of being an actor surrounded by palm trees and green juice rather than tundra and cheese. When I landed my first TV audition, my agent recommended his favorite acting coach. Noah came to my Sherman Oaks apartment. While we worked, he rubbed my dog’s belly, and I thought, “He looks really good for 50. But this was a professional thing, right? Maybe he would be my cool, older mentor. …” That failed, and we eventually went on a date and another. On our third date, Noah looked at me and said, “Hey. Do me a favor. Don’t Google me just yet.” Noah is a comic; he’d turn anything into a bit. But this time, he asked so sincerely, I knew it was important. Besides, Noah had thus far seemed pretty normal — well, for a person who didn’t want me to Google him “just yet.” I never felt at home in my identity until I met my new neighbor.
